cards.title: Dose-Normalized Concentration EDA Display Contract
cards.claim: Dose-normalized concentration exploration requires separate aligned panels for raw concentration (C) and dose-normalized concentration (C/D), preserving individual record status and experimental unit identity without inferring mechanism from visual overlap.
conditions: Applicable to observed concentration records with compatible dose, assay and sampling context; numerical normalization requires verified positive dose for the specific record.
Normalization applies only to records with verified positive compatible dose.
BLQ and above-range values are handled via status indicators, not substitution.
Visual similarity or divergence in C/D plots is descriptive and conditional on comparable study design.
required_inputs: Conditional input mapping: numeric values only for quantified records; optional summaries/errors only when shown; assay-specific or branch-specific fields only when applicable. Missing fields limit dependent operations, not all displays.
Record/source locator, study, design, observation ID, experimental-unit ID (nullable), specimen/pool ID, technical-repeat ID.
Regimen and dose occasion, route/formulation, analyte, matrix, free/total basis.
Time value/unit/origin, measured value/unit and quantification status.
Dose amount/basis/unit, exposure time origin, and whether denominator is per administration or period.
Nullable serial_observation_subject_id, distinct from experimental_unit_id (e.g. an animal within its randomized cage); required for individual serial lines or paired loops.
limitations: Unknown, zero, incompatible or ambiguous dose blocks that record's normalization only; such records are shown unnormalized with status.
Technical repeats do not increase biological n; unknown n or variability stays unknown.
No automatic confidence intervals or zero-width bars are generated; supplied statistics must have defined method and n.
This recipe is an explicitly reviewed engineering display contract, not a regulator-mandated layout or scientific law.
cards.downstream_use: Supports preliminary visual examination of population PK data to reveal patterns and features, serving as a diagnostic tool for confirming assumptions or suggesting corrective actions before model development.

plot_recipe.input_contract: Preserve record/source locator, study, design, observation ID, experimental-unit ID (nullable), specimen/pool ID, technical-repeat ID, regimen and dose occasion, route/formulation, analyte, matrix, free/total basis, time value/unit/origin, measured value/unit and quantification status. Map only available applicable fields; never invent missing identities. Preserve nullable serial_observation_subject_id separately from experimental_unit_id, with its source linkage. Numeric measured value is required only for quantified records; censoring/missing statuses may have a null numeric value. Optional summary/error inputs are needed only when that layer is displayed.
plot_recipe.plot_type: Separate aligned panels for raw concentration and dose-normalized concentration; zero-dose controls and unknown-dose records remain visible in the raw panel/status table.
plot_recipe.axes_and_units: X = documented time, unit and dosing reference. Y1 = C in concentration units; Y2 in a separate panel = C/D with units (concentration unit)/(dose unit). State dose basis and whether denominator is per administration or period. Use only compatible route/formulation/analyte/matrix/basis and regimen context.
plot_recipe.grouping_and_connections: Separate study, regimen/dose occasion, route/formulation, analyte/matrix/basis and endpoint contexts. Connect only verified serial observations of the same unit in a compatible time reference, ordered by time. Break connections at recorded unresolved missing/censored statuses. No invented scheduled samples or cross-unit lines. Serial-observation subject ID is distinct from experimental-unit ID: a cage/litter may contain several animals. Individual trajectories or paired loops require the same verified serial_observation_subject_id within study and compatible regimen/time/assay context. A shared cage/litter ID alone never authorizes connecting animals. Unknown serial identity blocks individual lines/pairs, not record-level displays; unknown experimental-unit identity blocks independent-unit n/uncertainty, not an otherwise verified observed subject series.
plot_recipe.point_and_summary_layers: Preserve observed values as points at their actual record level. Keep raw observations separate from optional source-reported or explicitly defined descriptive summaries. A labelled group-summary guide is not an individual trajectory. Do not reconstruct individuals from a mean and SD.
plot_recipe.censoring_and_missingness: Separate quantified, BLQ, confirmed above-range, missing, not sampled and technical-failure states. BLQ is not zero or negative. Confirmed BLQ implies C < LLOQ; confirmed above-range implies C > ULOQ. Default engineering convention: categorical status strip; optional boundary markers require known applicable limits and explicit inequality. No substitution or silent exclusion.
plot_recipe.transformations_and_formula: C_normalized = C/D only for verified positive compatible dose D. Preserve active-moiety basis and weight provenance for mass-per-body-weight conversion. Normalize individual records before summaries if dose varies: mean(C_i/D_i) generally differs from mean(C_i)/mean(D_i). For a valid numeric bound use LLOQ/D or ULOQ/D with its inequality; do not normalize zero or unknown dose.
plot_recipe.uncertainty_and_n: Label displayed record counts separately from known independent experimental-unit n. Preserve supplied statistic, calculation scale and exact SD, SE or CI meaning, including asymmetric interval endpoints. Technical repeats do not increase biological n. Unknown n or variability stays unknown; no automatic CI or zero-width bar.
plot_recipe.interpretation_limits: Overlap or divergence of C/D curves is descriptive conditional on comparable study design. It does not establish proportionality or choose a structural/covariate model; differences can involve schedule, formulation, sampling, binding, bioavailability or assay context.
plot_recipe.stop_or_fallback: Unknown, zero, incompatible or ambiguous dose blocks that record's normalization only. Show it unnormalized with status and exact counts/denominators; no invented 10% or other cutoff. Serial-observation subject ID is distinct from experimental-unit ID: a cage/litter may contain several animals. Individual trajectories or paired loops require the same verified serial_observation_subject_id within study and compatible regimen/time/assay context. A shared cage/litter ID alone never authorizes connecting animals. Unknown serial identity blocks individual lines/pairs, not record-level displays; unknown experimental-unit identity blocks independent-unit n/uncertainty, not an otherwise verified observed subject series.
plot_recipe.implementation_conventions: This recipe is an explicitly reviewed engineering display contract, not a regulator-mandated layout or scientific law. Use readable legends, separate aligned panels and visible status/count annotations. No universal numeric completeness threshold. No change to source data or current project Rules.

claim_support.claim: Preliminary examination of data using graphical and statistical techniques reveals patterns and features, serving as diagnostic tools for confirming assumptions or suggesting corrective actions.
In the cited Phoenix NCA documentation, Cmax_D = Cmax/Dose and AUClast_D = AUClast/Dose. These are software-defined normalized NCA endpoints, not a mandate for the raw C(t)/D plotting layout.
claim_support.scope: Software documentation for NCA parameter formulas.

claim_support.claim: The cited Phoenix discrete-data NCA documentation requires sample time and concentration inputs. Its N_Samples parameter excludes missing or non-numeric observations; that software counting rule is not adopted as an EDA deletion policy.
claim_support.scope: Software documentation for NCA parameter formulas.
